newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Iraq oil sale to cut prices $1.50/barrel - Arrieta.
newsitem.headline: Iraq oil sale to cut prices $1.50/barrel - Arrieta.

text.p: The forthcoming sale of $2 billion of Iraqi oil for humanitarian reasons will cause a drop in crude prices of up to $1.50 per barrel, Venezuela's Energy and Mines Minister Erwin Arrieta said Tuesday.
"In the worst case scenario we are talking about a $1.50 per barrel fall," Arrieta told reporters at a ceremonial event in Caracas.
Arrieta said the effect of Iraq's re-entry to oil markets through the United Nations oil-for-food scheme would be mitigated by low inventories in consuming countries.
"The effect will not be so big as to alarm us due to, among other things, the lack of stocks," he said.
Arrieta said heavy consuming countries would shortly begin building up inventories for the winter.
A recent storm threat on the U.S. Gulf Coast and a fire at Tosco Corp's Bayway, N.J. refinery, "has produced extra demand which favors us," Arrieta said.
Venezuela is the main crude supplier in the western hemisphere.
